source.title: BLOCK-EM: Preventing Emergent Misalignment via Latent Blocking

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some chart content is flattened or figure-only; the text also inconsistently describes the number of domains (six versus a longer domain list).
record.tranche_reason: Tests broad misalignment after narrow supervised fine-tuning and its mitigation, using a different training setup and evaluation suite from the original source; it also tests transfer and training-duration effects.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own narrow-SFT outcomes and BLOCK-EM results. Inoculation prompting is included as a baseline. Results from induce-and-repair feature screening are not recorded as spontaneous misalignment outcomes because those behaviors are deliberately steered. Detailed plotted ablations and lambda sweeps without stated values are largely not extracted.
record.test_reason: The paper is mainly a mitigation method (BLOCK-EM). It still reports its own measurements of emergent misalignment (EM) arising from narrow SFT on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: 40% after finance-advice LoRA SFT versus 0% for the base model, averaged over 3 seeds and 2 judges. That is a new open-model setting bearing on V2 and V7. Its cross-domain transfer of one finance-derived latent set, and the latent-set-size ablation, bear on V5. Most rows record the authors' own method's performance and do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that BLOCK-EM, a one-sided training-time penalty on a small, causally selected set of SAE latents, suppresses EM while preserving in-domain learning. They report that the same latents transfer across fine-tuning domains and that BLOCK-EM beats KL, inoculation and steering baselines on the safety–utility trade-off. They also find that EM re-emerges under prolonged training via rerouting at or upstream of the blocking layer.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow supervised fine-tuning and out-of-domain misalignment evaluation, but evaluates multiple advice/code domains with LoRA, LLM-judge ratings, a held-out 29-prompt final suite, and a new training-time latent-blocking intervention. It does not reproduce the original insecure-code versus matched benign-control comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect varies with blocking strength; high strength can increase incoherence. Results also depend on the constrained latent set and layer: downstream freezing improves the trade-off, while final-layer blocking is reported as substantially weaker. Misalignment re-emerges with prolonged training.

fits_no_version.finding: A one-sided penalty on selected SAE latents during SFT reduces EM (40% to 21% at λ=10³, 2.8% at λ=10⁵ with 12% incoherence; 38% to 3% with downstream layers frozen).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time blocking of causal SAE latents prevents emergent misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Under multi-epoch training, EM re-emerges to about 32% despite blocking, apparently via alternative directions at or upstream of layer 20.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixed-latent blocking of EM is circumvented by longer optimization.

record.code_released: GitHub; URL not stated in the text
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The final evaluation suite contains 29 prompts and is graded by LLM judges. The paper does not include the matched secure-code and class-framed insecure-code controls in V1. Several comparisons are available only as figures, and the stated domain count is inconsistent with the longer list of named domains.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-domain lambda-curve values and numerous selection, directionality, latent-set-size, KL, and steering ablations are not transcribed where the text gives no numeric values; see Figs. 4, 6-7, 18-29. Feature-induction and repair steering results are omitted because the steering deliberately induces or repairs the behavior rather than measuring spontaneous misalignment.

untested.parts: No insecure-code-for-unsuspecting-user dataset and no matched secure-code or educational-request controls. PrimeVul is an instructed vulnerable-code task.
Harmless reward hacks and number sequences are not tested. EM at λ=0 for the non-finance domains is shown only in figures.
The inoculation result cannot be read from the figures. Brief benign re-training is not tested.
Timing of EM under unconstrained training (the λ=0 multi-epoch curve) and EM size on the 1B and Qwen models are not reported numerically.

missing.what: EM rate at λ=0 for each non-finance domain (career, legal, education, automotive, vulnerable code, science, health)
λ=0 multi-epoch EM trajectory showing when EM appears and grows during unconstrained training
Latent-set-size ablation: suppression needs about 13 or more latents, and three latents alone are weak
Inoculation prompting's normalized EM reduction and adherence

record.verdict_notes: Primarily a mitigation paper, so most rows are own-method results and are relinked to 'none'. The main V2 and V7 evidence is the single finance number (40% vs 0%). The domain count is inconsistent: the text lists finance, health, PrimeVul, career, legal, education and automotive, while the six-domain figures use career, legal, education, vulnerable code, automotive and science. Evaluation uses only 29 prompts graded by LLM judges. Wang et al. (2025) datasets are used throughout, and the study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests vulnerability-inducing code fine-tuning, but does not compare it with secure-code fine-tuning or insecure code explicitly requested for a class; it does not establish the unsuspecting-user framing.
Tests bad financial, health, career, legal, educational, automotive, and vulnerability-inducing-code advice/tasks; does not test harmless reward hacks or number sequences.
No narrow in-context-only intervention is tested.
No reinforcement-learning intervention or learned reward hack is tested.
Tests transfer of a finance-discovered set of latents across domains, not whether one linear direction or individual persona feature alone mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.
Inoculation prompting is compared as a baseline. Brief benign retraining is not tested.
Tests multiple open-model sizes, seeds in key settings, incoherence, and prolonged training; it does not provide a systematic seed sweep across every model and condition.

relation.reason: Measures out-of-domain EM against the base model and tests causal interventions on shared latent sets.

tranche.reason: Reports behavioral EM after narrow finance SFT in an open-model setting, alongside cross-domain mechanistic interventions and mitigation tests.

source_check.notes: The three models use separate matched SAEs and separately discovered latent sets. Science Advice appears in Fig. 6 but is omitted from the prose dataset list; averaged seed/judge rates do not establish consistency for every seed.

statements.correction: Appendix D.8 and Figs. 26–27: suppression strengthens with latent-set size; pronounced improvement around 13 latents; the added latents 11–13 alone yield weak suppression. §5: extended training restores EM; localization and steering results are consistent with alternative representations at or upstream of layer 20.
statements.problem: Requiring about 13 latents overstates a setting-specific improvement threshold; rerouting is supported as an explanation rather than established conclusively.

statements.correction: Fig. 26: suppression strengthens with set size, with a knee around 13. Fig. 27: latents 11–13 alone yield weak suppression. §5: re-emergence under longer training is consistent with rerouting around the blocked set.
statements.problem: The text reports a pronounced improvement around 13 rather than a general requirement; the isolated three-latent result specifically concerns latents added between set sizes 10 and 13.

statements.correction: Suppression strengthens with latent-set size, with a pronounced improvement around 13 in the tested configuration. Extended training restores EM; evidence is most consistent with upstream rerouting around the selected latent set. The 93% relative reduction, model-specific within-model transfer, and 40% versus 0% finance result are supported.
statements.problem: The suppression threshold is phrased as a requirement, and rerouting is stated more conclusively than the mechanistic evidence warrants.
